Hi Naomi — quick first pass based on the forecast and typical token/cost profiles. See bullets below; I can drop the calc CSV into the Drive if this looks reasonable.

Assumptions (from Helio spreadsheet): peak QPS 125, median seq len 350, peak concurrent requests ~80, demo-day bursts up to 250 QPS for 10-20 minute windows. Model family: LlamaX-70B (service-verified).

Recommendation (APAC primary, EU fallback lanes):
- APAC dedicated pool (prod steady-state): 6 x H100-80GB nodes (sustained throughput)
- APAC burst/standby: 3 x H100-80GB on hot-standby -> immediate add during demo windows (auto-burst policy)
- EU fallback pool (warm): 4 x A100-40GB nodes (lower-cost fallback, higher latency, reserved for capacity failover)
- KV/prefix cache: enable prefix cache across region (~20% token savings)
- Autoscaling margins: target CPU/GPU util headroom 55-70% to preserve p99 latency

Latency guidance (p95/p99):
- APAC H100 steady: p95 <= 180ms, p99 <= 420ms (with continuous batching tuned to 16 tokens/batch)
- EU fallback (cross-region): p95 <= 420ms, p99 <= 1.2s (call out: network egress adds variance)

Ops runbook highlights:
- Canary traffic start at 10% for 48 hours, monitor cost/token and p99 latency; rollback to A100 EU fallback on sustained degradation >20% p99 over 30m
- Demo-day burst policy: pre-warm 200K token KV cache, enable burst lanes 30m before demo start, auto-scale thresholds tied to 90th-percentile queue length
- Billing note: standby H100 lanes are charged at 40% of on-demand while hot-standby; committed burst lanes can be negotiated for a 6-month window

Open items / asks:
- Need exact model config (quantized FP16 vs int8) from Helio for final memory footprint
- Confirm whether AI features (tool-calling/streaming) will increase token output significantly

Attachment: capacity_calc.csv (prelim numbers)

Irene/Ben — any immediate compliance/ops flags? If not, I can convert this into a short proposal and cost estimate for Helio to review by Mon 07/20.

Thanks,
Karthik

Thanks Karthik — this looks like a sensible starting point. Two quick compliance/regulatory items to flag before we commit APAC prod pools: 

1) Data residency:
- For SG/Tokyo pilot we must confirm whether Helio will send any personal data to Redwood. If yes, EU/UK DPAs don't apply but APAC jurisdictions (JP/SG) may expect local subprocessors disclosures. We need Helio to complete the short region-specific data flow matrix.

2) Evidence stack:
- Helio will need SOC2 Type II and an up-to-date penetration test report to sign in to Private/Dedicated stack. We can provide a SOC2 summary and evidence artifacts, but depending on Helio's procurement they may request full artifacts w/ redaction.

3) Key mgmt & encryption:
- If Helio requires customer-managed keys (BYOK) for APAC pilot, that adds ~2wk lead time to provision and test. Recommend we keep keys managed for pilot unless they explicitly ask otherwise.

4) EU fallback implications:
- Cross-border fallback will change data residency posture; include a flag in the gating checklist that requires Helio sign-off on fallback behavior and a documented fallback consent in the schedule.

I'll add a short compliance checklist and the region data matrix template. Can we ask Helio to complete the security_questionnaire_helio.xlsx and return it by 07/22?
